scope_gaps.note: The NHS rule sits in the insomnia self-help list and also covers smoking and alcohol; it is counted from going to bed, while the sentence says przed snem. The page was last reviewed 19 March 2024.

Abstract-only snapshot. The sources count from bedtime (going to bed); the sentence says before sleep. The 8.8 h figure is stated for avoiding a reduction in total sleep time only, not for other sleep outcomes, and the abstract does not say how it was derived.
The abstract does not describe how the 8.8 h and 13.2 h figures were derived from the pooled data; that would need the full text. The sentence does not say how.
The abstract says 24 studies were included in the analysis; it does not say how many contributed to each outcome.
The abstract gives no confidence interval, heterogeneity, comparator, dose or timing for the 45 min figure; it is a reported pooled outcome across studies with different doses and timings.
The source says at least 8.8 h and at least 13.2 h (minimum intervals, to avoid reductions in total sleep time); the sentence says a different interval without at least and without the outcome.
Abstract-only snapshot: no risk-of-bias, heterogeneity or certainty-of-evidence information to underpin the grade A, which is editorial and was not checked.

Intervals come from different documents with different aims: the NHS 6 h rule is a general insomnia self-help rule, while the Gardiner 8.8 h and 13.2 h figures are specific to coffee at 107 mg per 250 mL and a pre-workout supplement serve at 217.5 mg, for avoiding reduced total sleep time.
The abstract presents the 107 mg and 217.5 mg amounts as the basis of the two stated intervals, not labelled as examples; przykłady is the editors' framing.
